name: Luís Montenegro
role: Prime Minister of Portugal (Primeiro-Ministro), head of the XXV Constitutional Government
party: Partido Social Democrata (PSD), in the Aliança Democrática (AD) coalition with CDS-PP — European People's Party (EPP)
bio: Luís Montenegro (Luís Filipe Montenegro Cardoso de Morais Esteves), born in Porto on 16 February 1973 and raised in Espinho, is a lawyer with a law degree from the Catholic University of Portugal who has been Prime Minister of Portugal since 2 April 2024 and president of the Social Democratic Party (PSD) since May 2022. A municipal councillor in Espinho from 1997 and a member of the Assembly of the Republic for Aveiro from 2002 to 2018, he led the PSD parliamentary group from 2011 to 2017, the years of the troika bailout under Prime Minister Pedro Passos Coelho; he lost the 2020 PSD leadership run-off to Rui Rio and won the leadership in 2022. He led the Democratic Alliance (AD, PSD/CDS-PP) to a narrow plurality in March 2024; his first minority government fell on 11 March 2025, when parliament rejected a motion of confidence amid the controversy over Spinumviva, a company he founded with his family, and the AD won a larger plurality in the snap election of 18 May 2025, after which he formed the XXV Constitutional Government on 5 June 2025. As of October 2026 his governments have cut corporate tax and extended the youth income-tax regime, tightened the foreigners and nationality laws with votes from Chega while ruling out any governing agreement with that party, and approved the sale of 49.9% of TAP Air Portugal to Lufthansa; the prosecution service closed its preventive inquiry into Spinumviva in December 2025, finding no indication of a crime, while his dispute with the Entidade para a Transparência over public access to parts of his declarations is pending before the Constitutional Court.
